'''Joaquim "Quino" Colom Barrufet''' (born November 1, 1988) is a Spanish-Andorran former professional [[basketball]] player. Among other teams, Colom played for [[Baloncesto Fuenlabrada|Fuenlabrada]], [[BC UNICS|UNICS Kazan]] and [[Bàsquet Girona]].

==Professional career==
Colom played in the youth age categories with [[BC Andorra]]. He then played with [[CE Lleida Bàsquet|Lleida Bàsquet]], in the Spanish minor leagues, from 2003 to 2006. He made his debut with [[Basket Zaragoza 2002|CAI Zaragoza]] in the 2006–07 season, and then played with [[CB L'Hospitalet]] in the 2007–08 season. He spent the 2008–09 season back with Lleida Bàsquet and had another brief stay with CAI Zaragoza in 2009.

On 8 July 2009, he signed with [[Baloncesto Fuenlabrada|Fuenlabrada]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Fuenlabrada signs Quino Colom|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/77873/fuenlabrada-signs-quino-colom.html|access-date=11 July 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=8 July 2009}}</ref> On 31 July 2013, he parted ways with Fuenlabrada.<ref>{{cite news|title=Quino Colom, Fuenlabrada part ways|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/104413/quino-colom-fuenlabrada-part-ways.html|access-date=11 July 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=31 July 2013}}</ref> Two days later, he signed a one-year deal with [[CB Estudiantes|Estudiantes]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Estudiantes pens a deal with Quino Colom|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/104522/estudiantes-pens-a-deal-with-quino-colom.html|access-date=11 July 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=2 August 2013}}</ref> On 20 August 2014, he signed a one-year deal with [[Bilbao Basket]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Bilbao Basket lands Quino Colom|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/132078/bilbao-basket-lands-quino-colom.html|access-date=11 July 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=20 August 2014}}</ref>

On 11 July 2015, he signed a one-year deal with [[BC UNICS|UNICS Kazan]] of the [[VTB United League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Unics bolsters backcourt with point guard Colom|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/66wqokmgm9r3v9bt/unics-bolsters-backcourt-with-point-guard-colom|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150713032852/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/66wqokmgm9r3v9bt/unics-bolsters-backcourt-with-point-guard-colom|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 13, 2015|access-date=11 July 2015|work=Eurocupbasketball.com|date=11 July 2015}}</ref> On 18 May 2016, he was named the [[2015–16 VTB United League|VTB United League 2015–16 season]]'s [[VTB United League Sixth Man of the Year]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Quino Colom Wins Sixth Man Of The Year|url=http://www.vtb-league.com/en/news/quino-colom-wins-6th-man-of-the-year.htm|access-date=12 June 2016|work=vtb-league.com|date=18 May 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160531102647/http://www.vtb-league.com/en/news/quino-colom-wins-6th-man-of-the-year.htm|archive-date=31 May 2016}}</ref> On 12 June 2016, he re-signed with UNICS for two more seasons.<ref>{{cite news|title=Unics Kazan sign Quino Colom and Evgeniy Pashutin to a two-year contract extension|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/russia/201885/unics-kazan-sign-quino-colom-and-evgeniy-pashutin-to-a-two-year-contract-extension.html|access-date=12 June 2016|work=Sportando.com|date=12 June 2016}}</ref>

On July 14, 2019, Colom signed a two-year deal with Spanish club [[Valencia Basket]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Valencia lands former All-EuroCup playmaker Colom |url=https://www.euroleague.net/news/i/9sso4dfq7hhebcmn |access-date=15 July 2019 |work=EuroLeague.net |date=14 July 2019}}</ref> On 16 December 2020, he parted ways with Valencia and signed for Serbian club [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]] of the [[ABA League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Crvena zvezda mts get stronger by adding Colom |url=https://www.aba-liga.com/news/44286/crvena-zvezda-mts-get-stronger-by-adding-colom/ |website=aba-liga.com |access-date=16 December 2020}}</ref> He finished the 2020–21 season off by playing for [[Saski Baskonia]].

On August 20, 2021, Colom signed with [[AEK B.C.|AEK Athens]] of the [[Greek Basket League]] and the [[Basketball Champions League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=ΑΕΚ BC signs Colom |url=https://www.aekbc.gr/en/articles-3763/aek-bc-signs-colom.htm |website=aekbc.gr |access-date=20 August 2021 |archive-date=20 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211020160814/https://www.aekbc.gr/en/articles-3763/aek-bc-signs-colom.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 26 league games, he averaged 13 points, 3.6 rebounds, 6.3 assists and 0.5 steals, playing around 31 minutes per contest. On July 10, 2022, Colom parted ways with the Greek club.

On July 11, 2022, Colom signed with [[Bàsquet Girona]] of the [[Liga ACB]].<ref>{{Cite web |title='Quino' Colom fitxa pel Bàsquet Girona |url=https://basquetgirona.com/noticia/quino-colom-fitxa-pel-basquet-girona/ |website=Bàsquet Girona |access-date=2025-01-20 |date=2022-07-11 |language=ca}}</ref> Serving as the team's captain after [[Marc Gasol]] retired, Colom parted ways with Girona at the end of the [[2023–24 ACB season|2023-24 season]]. It was Colom's 11th season in the [[Liga ACB]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Quino Colom no seguirá en el Bàsquet Girona |url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/baloncesto/20240626/1002271316/quino-colom-seguira-basquet-girona.html |access-date=2025-01-20 |date=2024-06-26 |website=Mundo Deportivo |language=es}}</ref>

On February 25, 2025, Colom announced his retirement from professional basketball at age 36.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Quino Colom, el mejor jugador formado en Andorra, se retira
|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/baloncesto/20250225/1002414829/quino-colom-mejor-jugador-formado-andorra-retira.html |access-date=2025-02-26 |date=2025-02-25 |website=Mundo Deportivo |language=es}}</ref>

==National team career==
After playing an [[FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship|Under-16 Championship]] with [[Andorra national basketball team|Andorra]] in 2004, where he won the gold medal, Colom joined the junior national teams of Spain. With Spain's junior national teams, he played at the [[2006 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]], where he won a bronze medal, and at the [[2007 FIBA Under-19 World Championship]].

He also played at the [[2008 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]], where he was voted to the All-Tournament Team,<ref>[http://www.fibaeurope.com/compID_UIfgjyQcGqk-fPlnl66Tj0.season_2008.roundID_6087.coid_e-W9nS5yGPwOEXedgwlPW2.articleMode_on.html RADULJICA NAMED MVP.]</ref> and where he won a bronze medal.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20161002021440/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/lid_38135_cp/1/pid/41357/q/colom/rpp//_//players.html Quim COLOM (ESP) participated in 4 FIBA / FIBA Zones events.]</ref>

Thanks to his good performances during the 2014–15 season with [[Bilbao Basket]], Colom was pre-selected to play with the senior [[Spain men's national basketball team|Spanish national team]] during their preparation phase for the [[EuroBasket 2015]]. However, he did not make the team's final 12 man roster that competed at the tournament.

Colom was part of the gold medal-winning Spanish squad for the [[2019 FIBA World Cup]] in China.
